title: Finite nets supply a positive directional cover
hypotheses: D is a finite Euclidean delta-net of S^(d-1)
0 < delta < sqrt(2)
conclusion: For every unit v some u in D has <u,v> >= c = 1-delta^2/2 > 0; D spans R^d and |D| >= 2. Such finite nets exist for every delta > 0; one may arrange |D| <= (1+2/delta)^d.

title: Exponential barrier encloses an explicit inner tube
hypotheses: d is an integer with d >= 1; ambient space is Euclidean R^d
K is nonempty, compact, and convex; L = diam(K)
D is a finite subset of the unit sphere and a Euclidean delta-net, with 0 < delta < sqrt(2); N = |D|
epsilon > 0 and t > log(N)/epsilon
Phi(x) = sum_{u in D} exp(t*(<u,x> - h_K(u) - epsilon)); Omega = {Phi < 1}; C = {Phi <= 1}
conclusion: eta = epsilon-log(N)/t > 0 and K + B_open(0,eta) is contained in Omega; dist(K, complement Omega) >= eta.

title: Positive direction cover yields full coercivity
hypotheses: d is an integer with d >= 1; ambient space is Euclidean R^d
K is nonempty, compact, and convex; L = diam(K)
D is a finite subset of the unit sphere and a Euclidean delta-net, with 0 < delta < sqrt(2); N = |D|
epsilon > 0 and t > log(N)/epsilon
Phi(x) = sum_{u in D} exp(t*(<u,x> - h_K(u) - epsilon)); Omega = {Phi < 1}; C = {Phi <= 1}
conclusion: For p in K and R_p=max_{k in K}||k-p||, Phi(x) >= exp(t*(c||x-p||-R_p-epsilon)); Phi is coercive and C is compact, contained in closed B(p,(R_p+epsilon)/c).

title: Positive Hessian and strict convexity
hypotheses: d is an integer with d >= 1; ambient space is Euclidean R^d
K is nonempty, compact, and convex; L = diam(K)
D is a finite subset of the unit sphere and a Euclidean delta-net, with 0 < delta < sqrt(2); N = |D|
epsilon > 0 and t > log(N)/epsilon
Phi(x) = sum_{u in D} exp(t*(<u,x> - h_K(u) - epsilon)); Omega = {Phi < 1}; C = {Phi <= 1}
conclusion: Phi is real analytic with Hessian t^2 sum_{u in D} exp(t*(<u,x>-h_K(u)-epsilon)) uu^T positive definite at every x. Open chords between distinct points of C lie in Omega.

title: Closed sublevel and boundary identification
hypotheses: d is an integer with d >= 1; ambient space is Euclidean R^d
K is nonempty, compact, and convex; L = diam(K)
D is a finite subset of the unit sphere and a Euclidean delta-net, with 0 < delta < sqrt(2); N = |D|
epsilon > 0 and t > log(N)/epsilon
Phi(x) = sum_{u in D} exp(t*(<u,x> - h_K(u) - epsilon)); Omega = {Phi < 1}; C = {Phi <= 1}
conclusion: Omega is a bounded nonempty convex open domain, closure(Omega)=C, and boundary(Omega)={Phi=1}.

title: Analytic radial sphere parametrization
hypotheses: d is an integer with d >= 1; ambient space is Euclidean R^d
K is nonempty, compact, and convex; L = diam(K)
D is a finite subset of the unit sphere and a Euclidean delta-net, with 0 < delta < sqrt(2); N = |D|
epsilon > 0 and t > log(N)/epsilon
Phi(x) = sum_{u in D} exp(t*(<u,x> - h_K(u) - epsilon)); Omega = {Phi < 1}; C = {Phi <= 1}
conclusion: For p in Omega and each unit theta there is a unique rho(theta)>0 with Phi(p+rho(theta)theta)=1; rho is real analytic. theta -> p+rho(theta)theta is an analytic diffeomorphism from S^(d-1) to boundary(Omega). For d=2 this is a regular real-analytic Jordan boundary; for d=1 the boundary is two points. For d>=2 the outward-positive second fundamental form is positive definite.

title: Unit-vector identity improves the Hausdorff denominator
hypotheses: d is an integer with d >= 1; ambient space is Euclidean R^d
K is nonempty, compact, and convex; L = diam(K)
D is a finite subset of the unit sphere and a Euclidean delta-net, with 0 < delta < sqrt(2); N = |D|
epsilon > 0 and t > log(N)/epsilon
Phi(x) = sum_{u in D} exp(t*(<u,x> - h_K(u) - epsilon)); Omega = {Phi < 1}; C = {Phi <= 1}
conclusion: d_H(C,K) = sup_{x in C} dist(x,K) <= (epsilon + delta*diam(K))/(1-delta^2/2).

title: Tangential decomposition improves the numerator
hypotheses: d is an integer with d >= 1; ambient space is Euclidean R^d

title: Source planar analytic convex outer approximation
hypotheses: K is nonempty, compact, and convex in C identified with R^2
conclusion: There are bounded strictly convex open domains Omega_j containing K, with regular real-analytic Jordan boundaries, and sup_{z in closure Omega_j} dist(z,K) -> 0. The source construction at epsilon=delta and 0<delta<1 has error <= delta*(1+diam K)/(1-delta), and also the sharper bounds in ACOA-007 and ACOA-008.

title: Compactly nested neighborhoods with prescribed accuracy
hypotheses: K is nonempty compact convex in R^d
a_j > 0 and a_j -> 0
conclusion: There are bounded strictly convex analytic open neighborhoods Omega_j with d_H(closure Omega_j,K)<a_j, closure Omega_(j+1) contained in Omega_j, and both intersections equal K. At each step use m_j=dist(K,complement Omega_j)>0 and choose next error < min(a_(j+1),m_j/2).

title: Explicit source-style compact nesting schedule
hypotheses: K is nonempty compact convex; L=diam K
delta_1=1/2; delta_(j+1)=delta_j/[8(1+L)]
D_j is any finite delta_j-net; epsilon_j=delta_j; t_j=2 log |D_j|/delta_j
conclusion: The resulting barriers satisfy closure Omega_(j+1) contained in Omega_j and dist(closure Omega_(j+1),complement Omega_j) >= delta_j/4. Their closures converge to K in Hausdorff distance.

title: Exact interval barrier including singletons
hypotheses: K=[a,b] in R with a<=b
epsilon>0; t>log(2)/epsilon
m=(a+b)/2; L=b-a
conclusion: Omega=(m-rho,m+rho), where rho=acosh(exp(t*(L/2+epsilon))/2)/t; exact error rho-L/2 is strictly between 0 and epsilon.

title: Exact singleton radius for coordinate directions
hypotheses: K={p} in R^d; d>=1
epsilon>0; t>log(2d)/epsilon
conclusion: The exact Hausdorff distance from closure Omega to {p} is sqrt(d)/t * acosh(exp(t*epsilon)/(2d)). It is achieved on equal-absolute-coordinate diagonals.

title: Quadratic angular error for balls
hypotheses: d is an integer with d >= 1; ambient space is Euclidean R^d
K is nonempty, compact, and convex; L = diam(K)
D is a finite subset of the unit sphere and a Euclidean delta-net, with 0 < delta < sqrt(2); N = |D|
epsilon > 0 and t > log(N)/epsilon
Phi(x) = sum_{u in D} exp(t*(<u,x> - h_K(u) - epsilon)); Omega = {Phi < 1}; C = {Phi <= 1}
K is the closed ball centered at p of radius R>=0

title: Flat sets force linear angular error for finite directions
hypotheses: n>=4 is divisible by four
D has directions with angles (2k+1)pi/n, 0<=k<n
epsilon>0; t>log(n)/epsilon
conclusion: The finite-support polytope P_0 is contained in Omega, and (0,a tan(pi/n)) belongs to P_0. Hence d_H(C,K)>=a tan(pi/n), whereas delta_n=2 sin(pi/(2n)). A uniform quadratic angular error bound fails for arbitrary compact convex sets.

title: Convergence of maxima from outer Hausdorff convergence
hypotheses: K and C_j are nonempty compact sets with K contained in C_j
E_j=d_H(C_j,K) -> 0
All C_j lie in a common compact set Q
f is continuous on Q with modulus of continuity omega_f
conclusion: 0 <= max_{C_j} f - max_K f <= omega_f(E_j) -> 0. For M-Lipschitz f the error is <= M E_j.

title: Separate exact criteria for coercivity and Hessian positivity
hypotheses: D is a nonempty finite set of real Euclidean directions
t>0 and every exponential coefficient is positive
c_D=min_{||v||=1} max_{u in D}<u,v>
conclusion: The finite weighted exponential sum with slopes t*u is coercive iff c_D>0. If c_D<=0 then every nonempty strict sublevel is unbounded. Its Hessian is positive definite everywhere iff D spans R^d.

title: Singleton denominator is asymptotically attained
hypotheses: D is a finite set of unit directions with c_D>0
epsilon>0 fixed; t>log|D|/epsilon varies
conclusion: (epsilon-log|D|/t)/c_D <= d_H(closure Omega_t,{p}) <= epsilon/c_D, so the distance tends to epsilon/c_D as t->infinity. If delta is the exact chordal covering radius, c_D=1-delta^2/2.

title: Finite-dimensional analytic strictly convex approximation
hypotheses: d is an integer with d>=1
K is a nonempty compact convex subset of R^d
conclusion: There exist bounded strictly convex open neighborhoods of K with regular real-analytic boundary diffeomorphic to S^(d-1), converging to K in Hausdorff distance. These can be chosen compactly nested. No full-dimensionality of K is required.
